title: Aegis policy v1
description: Policy for Aegis Guard v1 (schema aegis.policy/1). All core fields are required; bash_allowlist is optional and defaults to [] and unknown fields are rejected. Aegis Guard reads this policy but does not install a host hook or enforce it.

schema.description: Policy format identifier. Must be exactly aegis.policy/1.

allowed_tools.description: Exact, case-sensitive tool allow-list. A tool not named here is denied. An empty list denies every tool.

denied_tools.description: Exact, case-sensitive tool deny-list. A deny here wins over allowed_tools.

allowed_roots.description: Path roots that may contain a path, file_path or notebook_path argument. Relative entries resolve against the repository; absolute entries are used as written. An empty list denies every path argument. Repository containment is always required in addition to an allowed root.

denied_paths.description: Additional glob patterns for denied paths. A pattern without a slash matches any path component; a pattern ending in /** also matches its directory; matching is case-insensitive. Invalid globs are policy errors (exit 3). Built-in secret patterns are always enforced in addition to this list.

deny_outside_repo.description: Boolean policy declaration. v1 always requires a path argument to resolve inside both allowed_roots and the repository; false is accepted but does not disable repository containment.

network_commands.description: Additional network command tokens to reject in a command argument. Matching uses shlex tokenization; built-in program basenames and the git/npm/npx/pip/pip3/uv subcommand rules are always enforced, and shell syntax, shell wrappers, and backslash/quote/dollar escapes are always denied.

required_session_files.description: Repository-relative files that must exist for the session command, in addition to .aegis/project.json. Entries must not be absolute or contain '..'.

bash_allowlist.description: Optional exact Bash command allow-list, default []. Bash is denied unless the command tokenizes (shlex.split(posix=False)) to exactly the same token list as one entry. No prefix or fnmatch matching. Shell and network heuristics can still deny an allowlisted command.
